shipped_promise_established_for_SC2: A mute one-directionally hides the muted account's content from the muter — its comments are filtered out of the muter's comment list and count, per viewer — and a block does everything a mute does plus cuts direct messaging between the two accounts in both directions; NEITHER stops the muted or blocked account from commenting on the other's video, replying to them, or seeing their comments.
shipped_promise_sources: internal/mute/service.go package doc: the mute package owns the model; 'the filtering effect on each content surface (comments, feed) is applied by those surfaces'
internal/block/service.go package doc: 'a block is enforced symmetrically: if EITHER user has blocked the other, direct messaging between them is refused in both directions'
api/openapi.yaml muteAccount: 'Mutes another account so its content becomes hidden from the caller'

api/openapi.yaml blockUser: 'direct messaging between the two is cut off in both directions, and the blocked account's content is hidden from the blocker … their comments are filtered from comment lists (per-viewer, exactly like mutes; other viewers are unaffected)'
internal/store/queries/comments.sql ListCommentsByVideo / CountCommentsByVideo: mute and block are viewer-scoped NOT EXISTS predicates on the READ path only; nothing on the write path consults either
vidra-user app/settings/mutes/page.tsx: 'Accounts you have muted. Their comments are hidden from you.'
vidra-user app/settings/blocks/page.tsx: 'Accounts you have blocked. Neither of you can send the other a direct message.'

SC1_owner_notification_privacy.implementation: One new :one query, CommentVideoOwnerRecipient, following the 0101/0103 set-based idiom already used by CommentReplyRecipient and NotifyFollowersOfNewVideo: the video's owner resolved with mute, block in BOTH directions, tombstoned comment (0057), federated comment (0053, NULL user_id), self-comment and inactive/deleted owner all as SQL predicates. NotifyComment now resolves its own recipient (actorID, commentID) → (recipient, error), mirroring NotifyCommentReply; it has to, because the caller cannot see the mute/block relationship. handleCreateComment keeps the mutual-exclusion check against the reply recipient using the video publicVideo already loaded, so the redundant second GetByID is gone.

SC2_blocked_muted_content_in_threads.not_a_gap: That a muted or blocked account can still comment on your video, reply to you, and read your comments is the SHIPPED promise, not a defect: mute and block are viewer-side hiding plus (for a block) a messaging cutoff. Nothing was redesigned.

SC4_deleted_or_tombstoned_parent.product_convention_established: There are TWO conventions behind one word. An author deleting their OWN comment is a hard delete, and comments.parent_id is ON DELETE CASCADE (migration 0026, whose own comment says 'Deleting a parent cascades to its replies'), so the replies go with it. The '[deleted]' placeholder with the reply thread preserved is the ACCOUNT-deletion path (migration 0057 / TombstoneUserComments): the row survives with an empty body and deleted_at stamped.
SC4_deleted_or_tombstoned_parent.author_deletes_own_comment: alice deleted her comment (204): the parent and bob's reply both left the list and the reply's row is gone from the database (cascade). alice's own comment_reply notification about that reply went with it — notifications.comment_id is ON DELETE CASCADE (0018) — so no notification survives pointing at deleted content. No API or UI leak of the deleted text is possible because no row remains.
SC4_deleted_or_tombstoned_parent.account_tombstone: dana hard-deleted her account (DELETE /auth/me, 204). Her comment survives as a tombstone: the API returns deleted=true, body '[deleted]', and an ANONYMISED author handle (deleted-<8 random chars>, per internal/account/delete.go) — never the original username. In the database the stored body is empty and deleted_at is set. bob's reply survives with its own body and its own attribution.
SC4_deleted_or_tombstoned_parent.browser: carol's watch page renders the tombstone as an italic '[deleted]' placeholder with no author name and no controls, and bob's reply below it under a 'View 1 reply' toggle, correctly attributed to bobu3 with its body intact. Screenshot sc4-tombstone.png, visually inspected.
SC4_deleted_or_tombstoned_parent.no_notification_for_or_from_the_tombston: Tombstoning dana's account created no notification for anyone (carol's count unchanged at 4 across the deletion) and dana's own notification rows are gone. alice then replied TO the tombstone: no new notification was raised at all — CommentReplyRecipient excludes a tombstoned parent, and the notification count referencing that comment id stayed at 1.
SC4_deleted_or_tombstoned_parent.residual_observation: That one surviving row is carol's pre-existing 'comment' notification about dana's comment, raised before the account was deleted. It carries no comment body (notifications never store one) and its actor renders as the anonymised deleted-<suffix> handle, so nothing of the deleted identity or text leaks — but it does mean a notification about a comment outlives that comment's tombstoning.

attempts_and_corrections: The first 'baseline' driver run silently hit the FIXED binary: the pkill pattern used an absolute path while the process had been started as ./vidra-api, so the old process kept port 8088 and the baseline exited with 'bind: address already in use' while healthz still answered 200. Caught because the baseline showed the fixed numbers. That run was relabelled as the fixed phase and the true baseline re-run after confirming which pid held the port.
The driver posted {"user_id": …} to POST /conversations; the contract field is recipient_id.
GET /me/blocks returns {"users": …} while GET /me/mutes/accounts returns {"accounts": …}; the driver assumed one shape for both.

The first browser walkthrough tripped the shipped 120 req/min rate limiter (35 x 429 in the API log), which put the comment list into its error state and made a later assertion read as a false negative. Re-run with 63-second cool-downs between phases and a hard failure on any 429, rather than by raising the limit.
No transcoder runs in this lab, so each fixture video was moved out of 'draft' with a direct UPDATE — a database fixture, not a code change.
unrelated_findings: components/CommentsSection.tsx fetches the comment list from a useEffect that fired before the session existed. The same 'fetch on mount, before the session is restored' shape may apply to other client-side reads whose answer is viewer-scoped; not swept here.

/settings/blocks describes a block as only 'Neither of you can send the other a direct message', but the API contract says a block also hides the blocked account's videos and comments from the blocker. The copy under-promises what the block does.

A notification about a comment outlives that comment's account-level tombstoning (it is only deleted when the comment ROW is, via the ON DELETE CASCADE on notifications.comment_id). Nothing leaks — no body is stored and the actor is anonymised — but the inbox row remains, pointing at a '[deleted]' placeholder.
